title: Consolidate the duplicated v2 InputBridge (Reacciona/Apunta) into shared V2 infrastructure
description: rev-t026 LOW-3 (TASK-026 review): the ~15-line v2->InputInterpreter bridge is duplicated in ReaccionaMicrogame and ApuntaMicrogame, and the copies ALREADY diverge textually — Apunta feeds normalized diagonal stick vectors (±0.7071 via DirectionToUnit) while Reacciona's ToStickXY feeds sign-pure ±1/±1 components. They behave identically today only because InputInterpreter.ToDirection8 classifies by axis sign alone; any future magnitude-sensitive change (e.g. a deadzone) breaks the two mechanics differently. Extract a single shared bridge type in Barcade.Core.Microgames.V2 consumed by both mechanics (and every future v2 microgame), define the canonical stick-vector convention (document whether components are sign-pure or normalized), and keep the zero-alloc property (bridge allocated once, array reference reassignment, no per-tick allocation). Do this only after TASK-025 and TASK-026 are closed so it does not race their reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one bridge implementation remains in Barcade.Core.Microgames.V2, consumed by both ReaccionaMicrogame and ApuntaMicrogame; the per-mechanic copies are deleted

The canonical stick-vector convention is documented on the shared type and pinned by a test (all 9 Direction8 values round-trip through the bridge into InputInterpreter identically for both mechanics)
Zero-alloc steady-state behavior preserved and re-verified through both mechanics' existing allocation sensors
Full fast suite green with no behavioral regression (both mechanics' existing tests pass unchanged)

comments.author: developer
comments.body: Delivered on master by dev-t101 (tests-after): e4cfc4b refactor(core) — shared Barcade.Core.Microgames.V2.InputBridge extracted, both mechanics' private nested copies DELETED -> 347cbae test(core) — AC2 regression locks (canonical convention pin, 9-value Direction8 round-trip through a REAL InputInterpreter, cross-mechanic check against a real ApuntaMicrogame). Suite 538 -> 544/544 (6 new). Both mechanics' _inputBridge field declarations needed ZERO changes (same type name, now resolving to the shared top-level type); straight before/after run confirms neither mechanic's existing suite — including both zero-alloc sensors (AC3) — needed a single edit (AC4). CONVENTION CALL (documented on the shared type): NORMALIZED unit vectors, not sign-pure — the cabinet stick is digital 8-way (GDD 1.3), so uniform magnitude 1 for every pressed direction is the physically honest representation; sign-pure's diagonal magnitude sqrt(2) has no hardware meaning and would make InputSnapshot's existing Magnitude()/WithDeadZone() read diagonals as 'harder pressed' if a deadzone ever lands — exactly the future magnitude-sensitive hazard rev-t026 flagged. ToDirection8 classifies by sign either way, so behavior is identical today. FOUND + DELIBERATELY LEFT (flagged): ApuntaMicrogame.DirectionToUnit carries the exact same values as the new InputBridge.ToUnitVector (Apunta's old bridge called it for input-bridging too) — judged merging them as scope creep (conceptually different roles: aim geometry vs raw stick reading); clean low-risk follow-up if wanted. SessionStateMachine's Loop/ surface untouched per constraint.

comments.author: rev-t046
comments.body:
FULL review verdict (diff 53a0622..347cbae, suite 544/544 verified firsthand in detached worktree at 347cbae, 538 baseline + 6 new): APPROVE-WITH-NITS — 0 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM (follow-up, outside AC scope, not blocking), 1 LOW (doc-only).

MEDIUM-1: a THIRD nested InputBridge copy survives at Loop/SessionStateMachine.cs:713-742 using the SIGN-PURE convention (ToStickXY, diagonals ±1/±1) — now contradicting the convention documented as canonical on the shared type. Behaviorally identical today (ToDirection8 is sign-only; no magnitude consumer anywhere), but it is exactly the latent drift hazard this ticket exists to kill, alive in one more place; its doc comment (705-711) also cites a duplication rationale this ticket just removed. Leaving it untouched here was CORRECT sequencing (file is in Loop/ under rev-t051's open review, and AC1 scopes to per-mechanic copies). Fix shape: follow-up ticket to replace the nested class with the shared V2 InputBridge (SessionStateMachine already consumes V2.PlayerInput[], likely drop-in) and delete ToStickXY.

LOW-1: ApuntaMicrogame.DirectionToUnit (V2/ApuntaMicrogame.cs:418) lacks a cross-reference doc comment ("mirrors InputBridge.ToUnitVector's values but is aim geometry, not the input convention — do not fold"); the intentional-independence rationale lives only in the commit message. Rides along with any next touch of the file.

DIRECTIONTOUNIT DISPOSITION: accept the leave-alone (with LOW-1's comment). The two tables coincide numerically but are semantically independent — the bridge's table is an input-representation CONVENTION; DirectionToUnit is ballistics GEOMETRY pinned by Apunta's solver tests. Folding them would couple projectile trajectories to the input convention — the exact bug class this ticket prevents. Scope discipline was right.

POSITIVE VERIFICATIONS (firsthand from pinned worktree): AC1 — exactly one InputBridge type in Barcade.Core.Microgames.V2, both nested copies deleted, both mechanics consume it, nothing shadows the top-level type, fresh unique .meta GUID. CONVENTION — normalized judged the right call against the GDD directly: §1.3 "exactamente 1 palanca digital de 8 direcciones... No hay ejes analógicos" (uniform magnitude 1 is the honest encoding; sign-pure's sqrt(2) diagonals encode a distinction the hardware cannot produce); §3.2 carries Direction8 enum at contract level so the float pair is adapter-internal; rationale documented on the type with GDD citation. REGRESSION SWEEP (Reacciona sign-pure -> normalized) clean: InputInterpreter.ToDirection8 strictly sign-based and is the ONLY read of bridge-fed StickX/StickY; Magnitude()/Normalized()/WithDeadZone() have zero production callers; both v2 mechanics route the bridge exclusively into _interpreter.Tick; other StickX/StickY readers in repo are v1 fed by hardware ArcadeInputBridge. AC2 — 9-value round-trip uses REAL InputInterpreter + real Tick; cross-mechanic check drives a REAL ApuntaMicrogame through all 8 directions; both pins discriminate (X/Y swap and dropped-diagonal both fail); convention double-pinned (±0.70710678 within 1e-6; magnitude-exactly-1). AC3 — both zero-alloc sensors byte-unmodified and strict; bridge allocates only at construction, For returns structs, no boxing. AC4 — both mechanics' existing test files absent from diff. Commit shape (tests-after) clean both directions: e4cfc4b production-only (type-name preservation verified), 347cbae test-side only. rev-t051 isolation verified: no Loop/ or Scoring/ files touched. Recurring HIGH-class sweep: nothing found.
